newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE to wander up to 4,275 then drift.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE to wander up to 4,275 then drift.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will make up lost ground on Tuesday and push its way up to around 4,275, technical analysts said.
Oil stocks should benefit from today's market strength whilst financial sector stocks will at least hold on to current levels, they added.

But analysts see dangerous times ahead and although the market should be free to roam higher today, sentiment could change rapidly. The market faces a stiff test later in the day as it awaits U.S. data which have the potential to create panic.
By 0712 GMT, the FTSE was indicated up 17.9 at 4,269.6.

Economists polled by Reuters expect the U.S. consumer prices index for March to have gone up 0.2 percent, and excluding the food and energy components -- because of their volatility -- it is forecast to have gone up by 0.3 percent.
Figures significantly higher than these will cause the FTSE to reel back this afternoon as fears of a further interest rate rise in the U.S. revive, analysts said.
The data will be released at 1230 GMT.
The FTSE has lost a little over four percent of its value since mid-March but it still looks vulnerable to a further assault by market bears over the near term, they added.
And yet the FTSE could make a swift comeback before being thrown off balance once more and the next few weeks may demonstrate that familiar pattern.
Meantime, a positive spirit should thrive but not so fiercely as to make the market's bears run for cover, analysts said.
